The `source` array fetches the official upstream release artifact from `https://github.com/nymtech/nym-vpn-client/releases/download/...` plus two local asset files (`nym-vpn.desktop`, `nym-vpn.svg`), all with pinned sha256 checksums. There is no top-level command substitution, no `pkgver()` function, and no code that executes at source time beyond ordinary variable assignments.

Running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will only download and extract these declared sources; it will not run `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()`. The `package()` function only installs the binary and asset files into `$pkgdir`, which is normal packaging behavior and is out of scope for this gate anyway. No suspicious network destinations, obfuscated code, encoded payloads, or exfiltration attempts are present. The pinned checksums further reduce supply-chain risk for the downloaded artifact.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard source array consisting of a direct HTTPS download from the project's official GitHub repository, along with two local files (desktop and SVG icon). The URL uses the `$url` variable which resolves to `https://github.com/nymtech/nym-vpn-client`, a legitimate upstream source. The binary is pinned to a specific release tag (`_release_tag=nym-vpn-v2026.12.1`) and includes a matching SHA-256 checksum, which will be verified during source integrity checks in later stages (though not during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, which only fetches sources).

There is no code in the global scope or in `pkgver()` that would execute commands, perform network operations, or exfiltrate data when the PKGBUILD is sourced. The `pkgver()` function is absent, so no dynamic version calculation occurs. All variables are statically defined, and no command substitution or eval usage is present. The `source` array uses direct, verifiable URLs without obfuscation or indirection.

Therefore, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will safely fetch the listed sources and parse the PKGBUILD without executing any potentially malicious code.
</details>
<summary>
No active code execution during source fetch
</summary>
</security_assessment>

The `Exec` line sets environment variables (`LOG_FILE=1`, `RUST_LOG=info,nym_vpn_app=debug`) before launching the `nym-vpn-app` binary with optional URL arguments (`%U`). These environment variables are commonly used for debugging and logging purposes in Rust applications and are consistent with the application's legitimate functionality.

There are no suspicious commands, network operations, or file manipulations present. The use of `env` to set environment variables is normal and expected for applications requiring specific runtime configurations. The `Icon`, `StartupWMClass`, and other fields point to appropriate application-specific resources, which is standard practice. No obfuscation, unexpected payloads, or malicious behaviors are evident.

This file does not execute arbitrary code, download content, or access sensitive system resources beyond what is typical for a desktop application launcher. It aligns with standard packaging practices and poses no supply-chain risk.
</details>
